chapters.title: Speech sounds, word stress and careful listening
objectives: Distinguish meaning-changing vowel and consonant contrasts.
Mark syllables and stress without confusing spelling with sound.
Use a partner and a dictionary pronunciation guide to improve clarity.
paragraphs: Pronunciation is the production of speech sounds so that a listener can recognise words. English spelling is an imperfect guide: one letter may represent several sounds and several letters may represent one sound. Listen to a model when one is available, repeat the whole word, and then use it in a sentence. This chapter gives text guides, not an audio recording. A teacher or partner can read the practice words aloud; do not claim to have heard a recording when you have only read its script.

A minimal pair consists of two words with one sound difference and different meanings. Ship /ʃɪp/ and sheep /ʃiːp/ contrast the vowels /ɪ/ and /iː/. The contrast involves vowel quality as well as usual duration: simply stretching every short vowel will not produce a correct long vowel. Say “The ship arrived” and “The sheep arrived”; context changes, but careful sound production also helps. Lip and leap offer another example of the same contrast.

Consonants can change meaning too. Thin begins with /θ/: let air pass between the tongue tip and upper front teeth without vibrating the voice. Tin begins with /t/, a brief complete blockage followed by release. This text description helps placement but does not replace listening to speech. For /ð/ in this, the voice vibrates. Accents vary, so use an intelligible model consistently and listen respectfully to classmates.

A syllable is a spoken beat. In the guides TA-ble and be-GIN, capital letters show the stronger syllable; they do not instruct you to shout. Stressed syllables are generally clearer and more prominent. TA-ble has first-syllable stress, while be-GIN has final-syllable stress. Write /ˈ/ immediately before the stressed syllable when using dictionary notation. Word stress can distinguish RE-cord, a noun, from re-CORD, a verb, in many English varieties.

Words can share a pronunciation while having different spellings and meanings. One and won are homophones in common English pronunciations. They are not minimal pairs because there is no sound difference between them. Read the whole sentence before choosing a spelling: “Our team won one match.” A dictionary may show both pronunciation and word class. Check the entry that fits the intended meaning rather than assuming a spelling always identifies a sound.

Use a feedback cycle: choose a contrast, listen to a model, speak, ask what the listener understood, and try again. A useful listener writes the word heard before seeing the speaker’s card. If a pair is confused, practise it inside a meaningful sentence before repeating the test. Keep a small record of the intended word, the word recognised, and the next step. Improvement means clearer communication; it does not require imitating another person’s identity.

examples.title: Vowel contrast in context
examples.problem: Explain the difference between “Please sit” and “Take a seat”.
examples.solution: Sit /sɪt/ contains /ɪ/; seat /siːt/ contains /iː/. The sentences have different grammar but both request a sitting position. Practise the contrasting words separately and then in their full sentences.

examples.title: Stress and word class
examples.problem: Read “Keep a record” and “We record results”.
examples.solution: In a common pronunciation, the noun is RE-cord and the verb is re-CORD. Meaning and position in the sentence identify the word class. Marking the stronger syllable helps the listener recognise the intended word.

examples.title: Choosing a homophone spelling
examples.problem: Complete: “Asha ___ the race by ___ metre.”
examples.solution: “Asha won the race by one metre.” Won is the past form of win; one is a number. The sounds alone do not distinguish these spellings, so sentence meaning supplies the answer.

chapters.title: Listening, paraphrasing and responding to messages
objectives: Take accurate notes from an original oral-message script.
Distinguish a requirement from a suggestion.
Paraphrase details and ask useful clarification questions.
paragraphs: Listening is active work: identify the speaker’s purpose, select useful facts, and check whether your understanding is accurate. Before a message begins, prepare spaces for who, what, where, when and action. On a first hearing, aim for the main point. On a second hearing, check names, quantities, changes and conditions. The original script below is written text for a teacher or partner to read aloud. It is not an audio file. Reading it independently practises comprehension but does not demonstrate listening ability.

Original announcement script: “Good morning, Form One. Our reading club will meet on Thursday at 3:30 in Room Four because the library is being cleaned. Bring a notebook and one book that you are willing to discuss; do not bring money. A book exchange is suggested for next month, but it has not been approved. If you cannot attend, tell Salma before lunch on Thursday. The meeting will finish at 4:15 so that members can catch the school bus. Thank you.”

The main message is the arrangement for Thursday’s reading-club meeting. Required actions are to bring a notebook and a book, and to notify Salma before lunch if absent. The room has changed because of cleaning; the announcement does not say the club has stopped using the library permanently. The exchange is a suggestion, not a confirmed event. Words such as suggested, must, may and has not been approved prevent a listener from turning a possibility into a promise.

Original follow-up dialogue script: “Juma: Did she say we should pay for the exchange? Rehema: No. She said not to bring money, and the exchange is only a proposal. Juma: I will be at the clinic on Thursday afternoon. Rehema: Then tell Salma before lunch. Juma: Can I send my book with you? Rehema: Ask Salma whether that is acceptable; the announcement did not explain it.” Notice how Rehema distinguishes stated information from a question that needs further checking.

A paraphrase preserves meaning in new words. “The club will use Room Four on Thursday while the library is cleaned” accurately restates the location and reason. “The library is closed for a month” invents information. A summary is shorter and selects major points; a paraphrase can be about the same length as its source. Neither should add an opinion disguised as a fact. Use quotation marks only when you reproduce someone’s exact words.

Responses should serve the purpose of the message. An acknowledgement confirms receipt; a clarification question identifies missing information; an action follows an instruction. “I cannot attend; I will notify Salma before lunch” is relevant. “Will the same room be used next week?” is a sensible question, but the answer is not available in this announcement. After listening, compare notes with a partner, return to the script to settle disagreements, and correct your own record.

examples.problem: Is the book exchange definitely happening next month?

examples.title: Paraphrasing an instruction
examples.problem: Restate “If you cannot attend, tell Salma before lunch on Thursday.”
examples.solution: Anyone who will miss the meeting should inform Salma on Thursday before the lunch break. The person, deadline and condition remain unchanged.

examples.title: An appropriate response
examples.problem: You are unable to attend. What should you say?
examples.solution: “Salma, I cannot attend Thursday’s reading-club meeting because I have an appointment. I am telling you before lunch as requested.” This reports the relevant action without claiming that sending a book is permitted.

chapters.title: Retelling events, explaining routines and giving directions
objectives: Retell an original story in a logical sequence.
Distinguish routines from actions happening now.
Give usable directions with landmarks and sequence words.
paragraphs: A retelling preserves the important events and their relationships while using the teller’s own words. Read the story, identify the difficulty, the response and the outcome, and then make a brief sequence plan. Do not memorise every sentence. A listener should understand who acted, why the action mattered and how one event led to the next. Words such as first, later, meanwhile and finally help when they reflect the actual order.

Original story, “The missing sign”: Every Saturday, Neema helps at the village reading room. One wet morning she found two visitors waiting outside the old store. They had followed a wooden sign that still pointed to the former reading room. Neema first greeted them and explained that the books had moved to the community hall. She walked with them past the water tank and stopped at the hall’s blue door. Inside, her friend Baraka was arranging chairs. Neema told him about the misleading sign. After the visitors had selected books, the two friends asked the caretaker for permission to move it. The caretaker agreed and checked the arrow before they fixed the sign beside the path. The following Saturday, new visitors reached the hall without asking for help.

The story uses the simple past for completed actions: found, greeted, walked and agreed. “Every Saturday, Neema helps” describes a routine in the simple present. “Baraka was arranging chairs” shows an action in progress at that past moment. When describing a scene now, use the present progressive: “Baraka is arranging chairs.” The choice of tense follows time and meaning rather than a rule that every verb in one paragraph must look identical.

Directions need a starting point, a destination and an ordered route. In the story, the route starts at the old store, goes past the water tank and ends at the blue door of the community hall. These landmarks are useful because a visitor can recognise them. Do not say “turn left” unless you know the person’s starting position and facing direction. A map and spoken instructions should agree; an unmarked shortcut can confuse a first-time visitor.

A routine timetable explains repeated actions with clear times. “On Saturdays, Neema opens the room at nine and sorts books at half past nine” is a possible new routine, not a fact stated in the story. Label invented extensions clearly. Possessives also help identify objects: “Neema’s notebook” belongs to Neema; “their books” refers to books associated with the visitors. An apostrophe marks possession in a singular person’s name but is not added to the possessive pronoun theirs.

Practise retelling to a partner who has not read the story. Speak clearly, use a manageable pace and pause between stages. Invite a question at the end: an unclear referent such as “he moved it” may need the names or object repeated. Then retell in fewer words while keeping the problem, response and outcome. Accuracy matters more than an elaborate performance that invents motives or events.

chapters.title: Reasoned group discussion and responsible online replies
objectives: Support and challenge proposals using evidence.
Manage turns with respectful verbal and non-verbal cues.
Write clear online replies without spreading unverified claims.
paragraphs: A group discussion aims to examine an issue and reach a clearer understanding or decision. A useful contribution states a position, supplies a reason and connects to what another person has said. Agreement alone does not prove a proposal is sound, and disagreement need not attack a person. Define the actual decision before debating it. “Which two afternoons should the club use the field?” is more manageable than “What is wrong with school sport?”

Original discussion script for a reader to perform; this is text, not audio: “Chair: We can use the field on two afternoons. Which days should we request? Amina: I suggest Tuesday and Thursday because our club has no lessons after three on those days. Paulo: Tuesday suits me, but the field is already booked for a match on Thursday. I checked the notice this morning. Amina: Thank you. Could we use Friday instead? Fatma: Friday gives us a second session, although some members attend the science club then. Chair: Let us check how many are affected before deciding. Paulo: I can ask them today and report tomorrow.”

The claim about Thursday is supported by Paulo’s stated check of the notice. The group should still confirm the booking with the responsible person before requesting a new arrangement. Fatma introduces a competing need rather than rejecting sport altogether. The final decision is postponed until participation information is collected. A faithful report must not say that Friday has already been chosen. Responsible speakers can acknowledge uncertainty while keeping work moving.

Use expressions that describe the relationship between ideas: “I agree with the aim because…”, “I see a difficulty with that date…”, and “Could we compare the two options?” Allow a speaker to finish before raising a hand or using the agreed signal. A relaxed posture and an attentive orientation can show interest, but eye contact and gestures have different meanings in different communities. Do not assume that a quiet participant lacks ideas; invite a contribution without pressure.

Online group replies need a clear reference because participants may read messages hours later. “About Thursday’s field booking: the notice says it is reserved for a match” is clearer than “That is wrong.” Before forwarding a claim, ask who issued it, when it was issued and whether the current source supports it. Avoid posting classmates’ phone numbers or personal explanations for absence without permission. A screenshot is not automatically reliable or current.

A chair can keep a decision log with proposal, evidence, unanswered question, action owner and deadline. At the end, summarise what was agreed and what remains open. An effective closing here is: “Paulo will ask science-club members today; we will review his report tomorrow. Tuesday is suitable, but the second day is not settled.” This helps absent members understand the discussion and prevents a tentative idea from becoming an invented decision.

chapters.title: Requesting services, negotiating prices and describing locations
objectives: Make precise, courteous service requests.
Use quantifiers and location expressions accurately.
Negotiate a price without misrepresenting agreement.
paragraphs: A service request explains what is needed and provides the details the provider needs to act. “Could you print twelve copies of this two-page notice, please?” is more useful than “Help me.” Add a deadline, ask about cost and check whether the service is possible. Courteous expressions include could you, may I and I would like. Politeness is not a promise that the answer must be yes; listen to limits and agree on a realistic next step.

Original shop dialogue script, supplied as text for role-play: “Customer: Good afternoon. I would like twelve exercise books for our study group. Do you have enough of the eighty-page ones? Seller: Yes. They are two thousand shillings each. Customer: That is twenty-four thousand altogether. Could you offer a lower price for twelve? Seller: I can sell the twelve for twenty-two thousand. Customer: Thank you. Does that include a bag? Seller: Yes, one paper bag. Customer: We can pay twenty-one thousand. Would you accept that? Seller: I am sorry; twenty-two thousand is my lowest total. Customer: Then we will take six today at the usual price. Seller: Certainly; that is twelve thousand.”

The customer checks availability before negotiating. The quoted unit price is two thousand, so twelve books normally cost twenty-four thousand. A proposed reduction is not a completed sale: the seller does not accept twenty-one thousand. The actual final agreement is six books at the usual unit price, costing twelve thousand. When paraphrasing, preserve both quantity and price. A confident tone should never turn a rejected offer into an accepted contract.

Quantifiers tell listeners how much or how many. Use many and a few with countable plural nouns: many books, a few bags. Use much and a little with uncountable nouns: much paper, a little ink. Some and enough can fit both: some books, some paper, enough books, enough ink. “A few books” means a small positive number; “few books” suggests an insufficient or disappointingly small number in many contexts.

Location descriptions should establish a reference point. Imagine a service centre with a reception desk just inside the entrance, a photocopy counter to the left of reception and a payment desk opposite the counter. “The payment desk is opposite the photocopy counter” names both the place sought and its reference feature. Left and right depend on orientation; tell a visitor to face reception first. Use near, beside, behind and between only when the arrangement actually supports them.

A request conversation usually opens with a greeting, states the need, clarifies details, negotiates if appropriate, confirms the agreement and closes courteously. If a provider cannot help, ask for an alternative instead of repeating the same demand. “When would it be ready?” and “Could you recommend another service?” move the exchange forward. Confirm the amount, quantity and delivery time before paying. Keep an accurate written record when the request concerns a group.

chapters.title: Combining oral sources and presenting a coherent report
objectives: Separate facts, estimates and recommendations in two original scripts.
Synthesise shared and differing information.
Use cohesive devices and intonation to present a balanced report.
paragraphs: Synthesis combines relevant ideas from more than one source around a question. It is not two unrelated summaries placed side by side. Start with a purpose, such as “What should our club recommend about the school garden?” Take separate notes for each speaker before grouping them into themes. Record who said what, because two speakers may use different evidence or speak about different times. Do not manufacture agreement to make a report simpler.

Original oral-source script A, gardener: “We planted forty bean seedlings on Monday. By Friday, thirty-four were standing upright; six had wilted. The bed beside the wall stayed damp longer than the bed beside the path. I think the path bed needs mulch, but we have not tested that idea. Please keep the gate closed because goats entered last term. I can demonstrate mulching on Wednesday after class.” This is a text script for a human reader, not recorded audio.

Original oral-source script B, student observer: “Our group counted thirty-five upright seedlings on Thursday, before Friday’s hot afternoon. We noticed that two watering cans leak. We have not measured how much water they lose. We recommend repairing the cans before buying more. Wednesday after class clashes with our debate practice, but two members can attend the gardener’s demonstration and report back. We should compare the two beds for a week before deciding whether mulch helps.” This second source is also original text for reading aloud.

The counts of thirty-five and thirty-four are from different days, so they are not necessarily contradictory. It is possible for one additional plant to wilt between observations; the scripts do not establish the cause. Both speakers favour practical action, but their priorities differ: the gardener proposes mulch and a closed gate, while students mention leaking cans and a comparison. The wall bed’s dampness is observed; the claim that mulch will help is an untested explanation.

Organise a report by themes: seedling condition, water management, animal protection and participation. A report might say, “Thirty-four of forty seedlings were upright on Friday. The gardener observed more lasting moisture beside the wall, while students found two leaking cans. We therefore recommend repairing the cans and comparing the beds before judging the mulch proposal.” Therefore signals a conclusion, while introduces a comparison, and before marks an order. Use each connector for a real logical relationship.

When presenting orally, group words into meaningful phrases and pause between points. In many varieties of English, a completed statement often ends with a falling pitch, while a genuine yes/no question may end with a rising pitch. Patterns vary with intention and accent; do not impose one pattern mechanically. Emphasise important contrasts, such as Thursday versus Friday, without shouting. End by distinguishing agreed actions, proposals and unanswered questions, then invite clarification.

examples.solution: No. The observations concern different days. One plant may have wilted later, but that explanation remains possible rather than proven. Report both dates accurately.

examples.title: A thematic synthesis
examples.problem: Combine the water-related information in one statement.
examples.solution: “The wall bed remained damp longer, and students found two leaking cans; repairing the cans and comparing beds would give the group better evidence for water-management decisions.” This combines observations without calling the mulch proposal tested.

examples.title: A logical connector
examples.problem: Connect “Wednesday clashes with debate practice” and “Two members can attend”.
examples.solution: “Although Wednesday clashes with debate practice, two members can attend the demonstration and report back.” Although correctly introduces a concession.

chapters.title: Usimulizi wa matukio: kiimbo, mkazo na mpangilio
objectives: Kusimulia tukio kwa mfuatano unaoeleweka.
Kutofautisha kiimbo, mkazo na lafudhi katika usemaji.
Kutumia sauti na mapumziko kuwasilisha maana kwa ufasaha.
paragraphs: Usimulizi ni utoaji wa habari kuhusu matukio kwa njia inayomwezesha msikilizaji kufuatilia wahusika, mahali, wakati na matokeo. Kabla ya kusimulia, panga mwanzo unaotambulisha hali, kiini chenye tukio kuu na mwisho unaoonesha kilichotokea. Usichanganye taarifa ulizoshuhudia na ulizosikia kwa wengine. Ukiongeza tukio la kubuni kwa mazoezi, litambulishe kuwa la kubuni. Mpangilio mzuri husaidia msikilizaji kuelewa sababu ya hatua fulani badala ya kukariri orodha ya vitendo.

Hadithi asilia, “Kikapu cha vitabu”: Siku ya Jumatano, Amina na Sudi walipeleka vitabu kwenye kona ya kusoma ya kijiji. Walipofika darajani, waliona maji yamefunika sehemu ya njia. Sudi alitaka kupita pembeni, lakini Amina alikumbuka onyo la kutokaribia mkondo wakati wa mvua. Walisimama mbali na maji na kumpigia mlezi wao simu. Mlezi aliwaelekeza watumie njia ya sokoni yenye daraja salama. Walifika wakiwa wamechelewa kwa dakika ishirini, lakini vitabu vilikuwa vikavu. Amina aliwaeleza wasomaji sababu ya kuchelewa. Baadaye, watoto walichora ramani ya njia salama na kuiweka ukutani. Siku iliyofuata, kikundi kingine kilitumia ramani hiyo kufika bila kukaribia maji.

Kiimbo ni kupanda na kushuka kwa sauti katika tungo. Kauli “Umefika.” na swali “Umefika?” zinaweza kuwa na maneno yale yale lakini zikawa na nia tofauti. Alama za uandishi hutoa mwongozo katika matini, ila sauti halisi hutegemea muktadha na kusudi la mzungumzaji. Katika usimulizi, sauti ya mshangao inaweza kuonesha hali ya ghafla; usitumie mshangao katika kila sentensi kwani tofauti za maana zitapotea.

Mkazo wa neno ni uzito unaowekwa kwenye silabi fulani. Katika maneno mengi ya Kiswahili sanifu, mkazo huwa kwenye silabi ya pili kutoka mwisho: ki-TA-bu, ki-KA-pu, a-me-FI-ka. Herufi kubwa hapa ni alama ya kufundishia, si sehemu ya tahajia ya kawaida. Mkazo wa tungo unaweza kulipa neno fulani uzito wa ujumbe: “AMINA alipiga simu” humtambulisha mtendaji, ilhali “Amina alipiga SIMU” husisitiza njia aliyotumia. Msisitizo huo hausababishi kubadili tahajia.

Lafudhi ni namna ya kutamka inayohusishwa na mazingira ya lugha ya msemaji. Tofauti za lafudhi hazimpi mtu thamani ndogo. Lengo la mazoezi ni kueleweka na kutumia matamshi yanayofaa kwa hadhira, si kudhihaki asili ya mtu. Matini hii hutoa maelekezo ya maandishi; haina faili ya sauti. Mwalimu au mwenzi anaweza kusoma mifano ili mwanafunzi asikilize, ajaribu na kupata mrejesho kuhusu uelewekaji.

Katika utendaji, simama au kaa kwa namna inayokuruhusu kupumua vizuri, tamka kwa kasi ya wastani na pumzika kwenye mipaka ya mawazo. Tumia “kwanza”, “baadaye” na “mwishowe” panapofaa, bila kuzirudia bila sababu. Unaporipoti sababu ya kuchelewa kwa wahusika, eleza kuwa walichagua njia salama; usibuni kuwa daraja lilivunjika. Mwombe msikilizaji ataje tatizo na suluhisho alilosikia, kisha rekebisha sehemu iliyoleta utata.

examples.title: Mpango wa masimulizi
examples.problem: Panga hadithi ya kikapu katika hatua nne.
examples.solution: Kwanza watoto wanapeleka vitabu. Kisha wanakuta njia imefunikwa na maji. Wanaomba ushauri na kutumia njia salama. Mwishowe wanafika na kuandaa ramani inayosaidia wengine. Mpango huu unabaki na tatizo, hatua na matokeo.

examples.title: Mkazo wa neno
examples.problem: Weka mkazo wa kufundishia katika neno kikapu.
examples.solution: Gawa neno katika silabi: ki-ka-pu. Hesabu kutoka mwisho: pu ni ya kwanza, ka ni ya pili. Kwa hiyo weka ki-KA-pu. Herufi kubwa zinaonesha mkazo tu; tahajia ya kawaida ni kikapu.

examples.title: Msisitizo wa ujumbe
examples.problem: Eleza tofauti ya “AMINA alipiga simu” na “Amina alipiga SIMU”.
examples.solution: Ya kwanza inasisitiza kwamba Amina ndiye mtendaji. Ya pili inasisitiza simu kama njia ya mawasiliano. Maneno yanaendelea kuandikwa kawaida katika matini isiyo na alama za mazoezi.

chapters.title: Kusikiliza mazungumzo na kuandika muhtasari mwaminifu
objectives: Kutambua maamuzi, mapendekezo na taarifa zisizokamilika.
Kuchukua dondoo kutoka hati asilia ya mazungumzo.
Kutoa muhtasari usioongeza madai mapya.
paragraphs: Kusikiliza kwa umakini kunahitaji kuelewa kusudi la mazungumzo, si kukumbuka kila neno. Jiandae kwa maswali: nani anasema, anazungumzia nini, lini na hatua ipi inahitajika? Sikiliza mara ya kwanza ili kupata ujumbe wa jumla na mara ya pili kuhakiki idadi, muda na masharti. Hati inayofuata ni maandishi asilia ya kusomwa kwa sauti na mwalimu au mwenzi; si faili ya sauti. Ukiisoma mwenyewe, umefanya ufahamu wa maandishi badala ya kuonesha uwezo wa kusikiliza.

Hati asilia ya mazungumzo: “Mwenyekiti: Tumekutana kupanga siku ya usafi wa kona ya kusoma. Neema: Jumamosi saa mbili asubuhi inafaa, lakini vitabu vihamishwe kwanza ili visilowane. Musa: Nitaleta boksi mbili. Hata hivyo, sijapata jibu la mwenye mkokoteni wa kubeba meza. Mwenyekiti: Basi tusitangaze kuwa mkokoteni upo. Asha: Tunaweza kusafisha rafu bila kuhamisha meza? Neema: Ndiyo, lakini sakafu yote itasubiri mpaka meza zihamishwe. Musa: Nitamuuliza tena mwenye mkokoteni leo jioni. Mwenyekiti: Tumekubaliana kuanza na rafu Jumamosi saa mbili asubuhi. Uamuzi wa kuosha sakafu utategemea taarifa ya mkokoteni.”

Katika hati hiyo, kuanza na rafu kumekubaliwa; kuosha sakafu kuna sharti ambalo halijatimizwa. Musa amesema ataleta boksi mbili na kuuliza kuhusu mkokoteni. Hajasema mwenye mkokoteni amekubali. Maneno “sijapata jibu” na “utategemea” yanaweka mipaka ya uhakika. Msikilizaji mwaminifu anayarekodi ili tangazo lisiahidi kifaa ambacho bado hakijathibitishwa.

Dondoo ni maandishi mafupi ya kukumbusha taarifa muhimu. Unaweza kutumia vichwa kama muda, vifaa, tahadhari, maamuzi na kazi zinazofuatiliwa. Andika “Jumamosi, saa mbili asubuhi; rafu kwanza; boksi 2—Musa; mkokoteni—jibu halijapatikana”. Hizi ni dondoo, si lazima ziwe aya kamili. Lakini muhtasari wa kuwasilisha kwa wengine unahitaji sentensi zinazoungana na kuonesha wazi uhusiano wa masharti.

Muhtasari hupunguza mazungumzo huku ukibakiza mawazo makuu. Ondoa salamu na marudio ikiwa havihitajiki kwa kusudi lako. Usiondoe sharti linalobadili maana: “Wataosha sakafu Jumamosi” si mwaminifu kwa hati. Muhtasari sahihi unaweza kusema kuwa wataanza kusafisha rafu na kwamba kuosha sakafu kutategemea kupatikana kwa mkokoteni. Tumia maneno yako, lakini usibadili mhusika wa jukumu au muda uliotajwa.

Unaposhiriki majadiliano, toa nafasi kwa wengine na uulize swali maalumu. “Musa, utatupatia lini jibu kuhusu mkokoteni?” ni bora kuliko “Vipi sasa?” kwa sababu linaonesha taarifa inayohitajika. Lugha ya mkato inaweza kutumika baina ya walio na muktadha mmoja, lakini rekodi ya mwisho ihitaji uwazi. Maliza kwa kuthibitisha maamuzi na kazi: ni nani atafanya nini na taarifa itapatikana lini?

examples.title: Dondoo lenye sharti
examples.problem: Rekodi hali ya mkokoteni kwa maneno machache.
examples.solution: “Mkokoteni: haujathibitishwa; Musa afuatilie leo jioni.” Dondoo hili linatofautisha kifaa kinachohitajika na kifaa kilichopatikana.

examples.title: Muhtasari sahihi
examples.problem: Fupisha uamuzi wa kikao kwa sentensi mbili.
examples.solution: “Kikundi kitaanza kusafisha rafu Jumamosi saa mbili asubuhi, baada ya kulinda vitabu. Kuosha sakafu kutategemea taarifa ya mkokoteni, ambayo Musa atafuatilia leo jioni.” Muda na sharti vimehifadhiwa.

examples.title: Swali la kufafanua
examples.problem: Je, mkokoteni utapatikana bila malipo?
examples.solution: Hati haisemi kuhusu malipo. Swali linalofaa ni “Je, mwenye mkokoteni atahitaji malipo, na kama ndiyo, kiasi gani?” Usijibu kuwa ni bure bila taarifa.

chapters.title: Mazungumzo ya nyumbani, shuleni na hospitalini
objectives: Kuteua msamiati na kiwango cha urasmi kulingana na muktadha.
Kutoa maombi, maelezo na hoja kwa adabu.
Kutumia tafsida bila kuficha taarifa muhimu.
paragraphs: Muktadha ni jumla ya mazingira yanayoathiri namna ya kuwasiliana: mahali, uhusiano wa washiriki, umri, kusudi na hali ya tukio. Kauli inayotosha kwa rafiki wa karibu inaweza kutofaa katika ombi rasmi. Hii haimaanishi kuwa kila mzee au kila kijana atapenda mtindo uleule. Sikiliza mwitikio wa unayezungumza naye na rekebisha maneno yako kwa heshima. Ufasaha ni kueleza jambo kwa uwazi na mtiririko unaofaa, si kutumia maneno magumu bila sababu.

Mazungumzo asilia ya nyumbani: “Mtoto: Shikamoo, bibi. Naomba nikusaidie kupanga vyombo. Bibi: Marahaba. Asante; weka vikombe hapa, lakini usibebe sufuria yenye maji moto. Mtoto: Nimeelewa. Nitaanza na vikombe vilivyopoa.” Salamu hiyo inafaa katika jamii nyingi zinazotumia Shikamoo; desturi zinaweza kutofautiana. Msaidizi amethibitisha alichoelewa na kutambua mpaka wa usalama badala ya kusema tu “sawa” bila hatua iliyo wazi.

Mazungumzo asilia shuleni: “Mwanafunzi: Samahani, mwalimu. Naomba muda wa ziada wa kuwasilisha kazi. Nilifika nyumbani nikakuta daftari langu limeloweshwa na maji. Mwalimu: Unaweza kuleta nakala mpya kesho kabla ya kipindi cha kwanza? Mwanafunzi: Ndiyo. Je, nikamilishe maswali yote au yale yaliyoharibika tu? Mwalimu: Yote, ili niwe na kazi kamili.” Ombi linatoa sababu inayoweza kufuatiliwa, linakubali sharti na linauliza ufafanuzi. Haliwahakikishii wengine kuwa kila ombi la kuongeza muda litakubaliwa.

Mazungumzo asilia hospitalini: “Mgonjwa: Habari, naomba kuelekezwa sehemu ya mapokezi. Mhudumu: Iko mbele, karibu na mlango wa kijani. Mgonjwa: Asante. Nimekuwa na maumivu ya tumbo tangu jana; nitamweleza nani? Mhudumu: Mweleze mhudumu wa mapokezi akuelekeze hatua inayofuata.” Lugha ya heshima haipaswi kuficha dalili muhimu. Matini hii ni mazoezi ya lugha; uamuzi wa huduma hutolewa na wahudumu wa afya kwa hali ya mgonjwa.

Tafsida ni uteuzi wa maneno ya upole badala ya maneno yanayoweza kukera au kuumiza. “Amefariki” mara nyingi hutumiwa kwa upole kuhusu kifo. Hata hivyo, upole usilete utata unaozuia msaada. Katika maelezo ya tatizo, taja kinachohitajika, kilichotokea na muda wake kwa namna inayofaa. Epuka matusi, ubaguzi na kudhani kwamba jinsia au umri wa mtu humpa tabia fulani moja kwa moja.

Malumbano ya hoja ni kuchunguza mitazamo kwa sababu na ushahidi. “Ninapendekeza rafu ya ziada kwa sababu vitabu ishirini vimewekwa sakafuni” ina hoja inayoweza kukaguliwa. “Mtu yeyote asiyekubaliana hajui kitu” ni shambulio, si ushahidi. Unapokataa, eleza sehemu unayokataa na sababu, kisha pendekeza njia mbadala. Malizia mazungumzo kwa kuthibitisha hatua inayofuata, kutoa shukrani au kufunga mjadala kwa adabu.

examples.title: Ombi lenye sababu
examples.problem: Boresha “Nipe muda mwingine!” katika muktadha wa shule.
examples.solution: “Samahani, mwalimu. Naomba kuwasilisha nakala mpya kesho kwa sababu daftari langu limeloweshwa. Je, muda huo utakufaa?” Ombi linataja hitaji, sababu na uwezekano wa kukubaliwa.

examples.title: Ufafanuzi wa maelekezo
examples.problem: Mwanafunzi afanye nini baada ya kupewa muda wa kesho?
examples.solution: Aulize iwapo atawasilisha maswali yote au yaliyoharibika tu. Baada ya jibu, athibitishe: “Nitaleta kazi yote kesho kabla ya kipindi cha kwanza.” Hii inazuia tafsiri mbili.

examples.title: Pingamizi la heshima
examples.problem: Pinga kununua rafu bila kuchunguza mahitaji.
examples.solution: “Nakubaliana kuwa vitabu vinahitaji sehemu nzuri. Hata hivyo, ningependa tuhesabu nafasi iliyopo kwanza ili tujue ukubwa wa rafu tunaohitaji.” Kauli inaheshimu lengo na kuhoji hatua kwa sababu.

chapters.title: Kusikiliza kwa udadisi na kuandika kumbukumbu za hoja
objectives: Kutofautisha taarifa, pendekezo na uamuzi katika habari changamani.
Kuuliza maswali yanayojaza mapengo ya taarifa.
Kuandika kumbukumbu zenye maamuzi, majukumu na muda wa utekelezaji.
paragraphs: Kusikiliza kwa udadisi ni kufuatilia ujumbe huku ukichunguza chanzo, maana na mapengo yake. Si kukatiza kila sentensi wala kukubali kila dai kwa sababu limesemwa kwa kujiamini. Andaa jedwali la hoja, ushahidi uliotajwa, swali na hatua. Unaposikia idadi, rekodi kipimo na kipindi chake: ndoo kumi kwa siku si sawa na ndoo kumi kwa wiki. Kama taarifa haijatolewa, andika kuwa haijatajwa badala ya kubuni jibu.

Hati asilia ya habari ya kusomwa kwa sauti; hii ni matini, si rekodi ya sauti: “Mratibu: Katika wiki iliyopita, wanafunzi walikusanya chupa mia moja na ishirini kutoka eneo la shule. Sabini zilipatikana karibu na uwanja, thelathini karibu na kantini na ishirini nyuma ya madarasa. Mlezi: Idadi hizo zinaonesha mahali pa kuanzia, lakini hatujui kama chupa zote zilitupwa wiki hiyo. Mwanafunzi: Ninapendekeza vyombo vitatu vya kukusanyia chupa viwekwe karibu na uwanja. Mhasibu: Tuna pesa za kununua vyombo viwili tu kwa sasa. Mratibu: Basi kamati ichunguze bei na njia ya kupata chombo cha tatu. Tusifanye ununuzi leo.”

Mwendelezo wa hati asilia: “Mwanafunzi: Je, chupa zitauzwa ili kupata fedha? Mlezi: Bado hatujathibitisha mnunuzi wala bei. Kwanza tutauliza wakusanyaji wawili wenye huduma inayoruhusiwa. Mratibu: Rehema na Doto watauliza bei za vyombo na kuleta taarifa Ijumaa. Mimi nitawasiliana na wakusanyaji kabla ya kikao hicho. Tumeamua kuanza kuhesabu chupa kila siku kutoka Jumatatu ijayo ili tujue mabadiliko. Mhasibu: Nitaandaa daftari lenye tarehe, eneo na idadi. Mlezi: Chupa zilizovunjika zishughulikiwe na mtu mzima mwenye vifaa vinavyofaa; wanafunzi wasiziokote kwa mikono.”

Taarifa iliyopo ni kwamba chupa 120 zilikusanywa wiki iliyopita; haijathibitishwa kuwa zote zilitupwa katika wiki hiyo. Pendekezo la vyombo vitatu halijawa agizo la kununua, kwa sababu fedha zinatosha viwili na kamati imeagizwa kuchunguza. Dai kwamba chupa zitauzwa kwa faida fulani pia halina msingi katika hati. Udadisi unahitaji kuuliza kuhusu mnunuzi, bei, gharama na usalama bila kudhani majibu.

Kumbukumbu za kikao si nakala ya kila neno. Zihifadhi mada, taarifa muhimu, maamuzi, majukumu na muda. Kwa mfano: “Rehema na Doto wachunguze bei za vyombo; taarifa Ijumaa.” “Mratibu awasiliane na wakusanyaji kabla ya kikao cha Ijumaa.” “Kuhesabu chupa kila siku kuanze Jumatatu ijayo.” Usiongeze tarehe ya kalenda ambayo haikutajwa; unaweza kuiacha wazi ili mratibu aiweke baada ya kuithibitisha.

Wasilisha mawazo makuu kwa uwazi na uwekevu. Uwekevu hapa ni kutumia maneno yanayotosha bila marudio yanayoficha ujumbe. Kwanza eleza hali, kisha tofauti kati ya kilichoamuliwa na kinachochunguzwa, halafu majukumu. Unapopokea swali la idadi, rudi kwenye dondoo: 70 + 30 + 20 = 120. Kujumlisha kunahakiki ulinganifu wa takwimu, lakini hakuthibitishi peke yake kwamba ukusanyaji ulifanywa kwa usahihi.

chapters.title: Kusoma kwa kina: ushahidi, maoni na muhtasari wa matini ndefu
objectives: Kuchunguza hoja za matini ndefu kwa kuzingatia ushahidi na mipaka yake.
Kutofautisha wazo kuu na mfano wake.
Kuandika muhtasari na maoni yanayoungwa mkono na matini.
paragraphs: Usomaji wa kina ni kufuatilia mawazo, uhusiano wake na namna mwandishi anavyoyaunga mkono. Kwanza pitia kichwa na muundo ili kutambua suala kuu. chapters.title: Mitindo ya mazungumzo, ishara na sentensi zilizounganishwa
objectives: Kurekebisha mtindo wa mazungumzo kulingana na uhusiano na kusudi.
Kutumia ishara zinazosaidia ujumbe bila kudhani maana yake kwa kila mtu.
Kutofautisha na kutumia sentensi ambatani na changamani katika mazungumzo.
paragraphs: Mtindo wa mazungumzo hutokana na uteuzi wa maneno, urefu wa kauli, kiwango cha urasmi na namna ya kubadilishana zamu. Mazungumzo ya marafiki yanaweza kuwa na kauli fupi kwa sababu wana taarifa za pamoja. Katika huduma rasmi, maelezo kamili husaidia mtu asiyejua hali yako. Umri, uhusiano na mazingira yanaweza kuathiri uteuzi, lakini usidhanie kwamba jinsia au umri humlazimisha kila mtu kupenda mtindo mmoja. Uliza na sikiliza kwa heshima.

Hati asilia ya mazungumzo ya marafiki: “Tunu: Umeona mpira? Kito: Upo kwa mlezi. Tuombe kabla ya mazoezi. Tunu: Sawa; nitamuuliza kama tunaweza kuutumia hadi saa kumi na moja. Kito: Ukiruhusiwa, niambie, nami nitawaita wenzetu.” Hati asilia ya ombi kwa mlezi: “Tunu: Shikamoo, mlezi. Naomba tuutumie mpira kwa mazoezi hadi saa kumi na moja, ikiwa uwanja uko wazi. Mlezi: Marahaba. Mnaweza kuutumia, lakini uwanja unahitajika saa kumi na nusu. Tunu: Asante; basi tutamaliza na kurudisha mpira kabla ya saa kumi na nusu.” Hizi ni hati za maandishi kwa maigizo, si sauti iliyorekodiwa.

Tunu anabadilisha mtindo bila kubadili ukweli wa hitaji lake. Kwa rafiki ametumia “Sawa” na rejea fupi; kwa mlezi ametaja ombi, mwisho wa muda na sharti la uwanja. Jibu la mlezi linaweka mpaka mpya wa saa kumi na nusu. Kurudia mpango uliorekebishwa kunaonesha uelewano. Kama Tunu angewaambia wenzake kuwa wamepewa hadi saa kumi na moja, angekuwa amepuuza sharti lililotolewa.

Ishara zinaweza kusaidia ujumbe: kuinua mkono kuomba zamu, kuonesha sehemu kwenye mchoro au kutikisa kichwa kuonesha kuwa unasikiliza. Hata hivyo, maana hutegemea jamii na muktadha. Kutikisa kichwa hakuthibitishi kila mara makubaliano; huenda ni ishara ya kufuatilia. Ikiwa uamuzi ni muhimu, thibitisha kwa maneno. Heshimu nafasi ya mtu na hitaji lake la kutotazamwa moja kwa moja; usilazimishe ishara moja kama kipimo pekee cha heshima.

Sentensi ambatani huunganisha vishazi huru viwili au zaidi: “Tunu atauliza ruhusa, na Kito atawaita wenzake.” Kila kishazi kinaweza kusimama kama taarifa kamili. Sentensi changamani ina kishazi kikuu na kishazi tegemezi: “Mkipata ruhusa, anzeni mazoezi.” Sehemu “mkipata ruhusa” hutoa sharti na haiwasilishi ujumbe kamili wa kujitegemea katika matumizi hayo. Viunganishi na viambishi vya masharti viwe na uhusiano wa maana, si mapambo ya kuifanya sentensi ionekane ndefu.

Fanya mazoezi ya kuanzisha, kuingilia kwa ruhusa, kubadili mada na kufunga mazungumzo. “Samahani kwa kuingilia; naomba kuthibitisha muda” husaidia kurekebisha jambo muhimu. “Kabla hatujamaliza, tuweke wazi nani atarudisha mpira” huleta hatua ya mwisho. Tumia sauti na ishara zinazolingana na maneno, halafu hakiki maana kwa kurudia makubaliano. Mazungumzo yenye mafanikio huwaacha washiriki wakijua kilichoombwa, kilichokubaliwa na kinachohitajika kufanywa.
